text:
I’m a tourist from France, and before coming to New York, I did some research on the places you supposedly “shouldn’t miss.” Joe’s Pizza at 1435 Broadway was one of them.
I had seen information suggesting that pizza slices were around $2. Let me be very clear: that was absolutely not my experience.
As a European and someone familiar with Italian food, I know what a simple cheese pizza is supposed to be: straightforward, good-quality ingredients, proper cheese, and a good crust. What I was served here was honestly disgusting. The cheese was like mush, the quality was extremely disappointing, and it was nothing like the famous New York pizza experience I had been expecting.
What bothered me even more was the feeling that tourists are simply there to be rushed through, served whatever they are given, and charged. I did not feel welcomed or valued as a customer at all. It felt like: pay, eat, and get out.
Maybe Joe’s Pizza earned its reputation many years ago, but I’m writing this review as a tourist visiting New York in 2026, and based on my personal experience, I simply do not understand the hype.
For such a famous name, serving pizza of this quality and treating tourists this way is a real shame.
Very disappointing experience. I cannot recommend this place, and personally, I would avoid it.

text:
I had a great experience at this Vietnamese restaurant and would definitely recommend it. The first thing that stood out was the modern, tasteful décor. The atmosphere feels stylish without being overdone, making it equally suitable for a quick business lunch, a casual meal with friends, or a relaxed family dinner. It’s one of those places where you immediately feel comfortable.

The menu is another highlight. Instead of offering only the standard Vietnamese dishes you find almost everywhere, they have a well-rounded selection with plenty of interesting options. Whether you’re visiting for the first time or already love Vietnamese cuisine, there’s enough variety to keep you coming back and trying something new.

A special mention has to go to the drinks. If you appreciate freshly made beverages, this is the place to visit. They are clearly prepared to order, taste incredibly fresh, and pair perfectly with the food. It’s refreshing to see a restaurant put as much care into its drinks as it does into the menu.

The portions are also very generous, so you definitely get good value for your money. Despite the generous serving sizes, the food arrived surprisingly quickly, making it an excellent choice if you’re on a lunch break or simply don’t want to wait too long. Most importantly, everything tasted fresh and well prepared.

Overall, this is a fantastic Vietnamese restaurant that combines a welcoming atmosphere, excellent food, fresh drinks, generous portions, and efficient service. It’s a place I’ll happily return to and would recommend to anyone looking for something beyond the typical Vietnamese restaurant experience.

It is the epitome of the classic Schweinshaxen.

It is not salty, yet tender and crispy; pairing it with beer makes all your fatigue melt away.

I had tried German restaurants a few times before, but I hesitated because they were too salty and tough for me.

Based on a good memory, I visited a restaurant in Frankfurt recommended by someone, but it didn't suit my taste.

The portions are large, so you need to be careful with your order.

Located beneath the train station, the acoustics were great when trains passed by, and the interior atmosphere also contributes to the dining experience.

text:
Here’s a polished version of your review that keeps your strong negative opinion while making it more structured, credible, and impactful:

⸻

★☆☆☆☆ – One of the Most Disappointing Michelin Experiences I’ve Ever Had

I genuinely do not understand how Restaurant Facil holds two Michelin stars. Having dined at many Michelin-starred restaurants, this was easily one of the most underwhelming experiences I’ve had.

The problems started with the service. While one or two servers were genuinely warm and professional, the majority came across as cold, unengaged, and uninterested in communicating. Basic English seemed to be a challenge for several members of the team, making it difficult for them to explain the dishes. At this level, every course should be introduced with confidence and enthusiasm. Instead, it often felt awkward and uninformed.

Even before arriving, there were signs that attention to detail was lacking. On the day of our reservation, Google Maps listed the restaurant as “Temporarily Closed.” For a two-Michelin-star establishment, this is the sort of basic operational detail that should never be overlooked. When I mentioned it to the staff, my feedback was simply brushed aside, reflecting an unfortunate lack of care.

As for the food, it was astonishingly ordinary. There was nothing memorable, innovative, or technically impressive about most of the menu. It felt like standard Western cuisine without any creativity or ambition. Rather than highlighting the quality of the ingredients, many dishes were excessively salty, masking their natural flavours with seasoning. I kept waiting for a course that would justify the restaurant’s reputation, but it never came.

The only exception was the dessert course. Here, the kitchen finally showed some imagination, with creative presentations and a touch of theatricality. Unfortunately, one good dessert course cannot redeem an otherwise forgettable meal.

The dining environment also left much to be desired. The restaurant features a retractable roof, which is undoubtedly beautiful when open. However, it remained closed for most of our nearly three-hour meal, leaving the room feeling stuffy with stagnant air. It was only opened towards the very end, by which point it made little difference to the overall experience.

Ultimately, this meal felt like a complete waste of both time and money. I left wondering not what I had enjoyed, but how this restaurant earned—and continues to hold—two Michelin stars. Aside from the desserts and the potential beauty of the venue when the roof is open, I found very little to recommend.

I’ve had exceptional experiences at Michelin-starred restaurants around the world, so my expectations were high. Restaurant Facil fell dramatically short of them. Unfortunately, this ranks among the worst Michelin dining experiences I’ve had.

text:
We had been looking forward to the chic dinner at Facil in Berlin, awarded 2 Michelin stars, for quite some time. Because we do not eat meat, we opted for the vegetarian menu, which is slightly cheaper than the regular menu. We chose the 7-course menu once and the 8-course menu once. The dining room is beautifully situated on an upper floor of the hotel, though there is no view. To create a garden atmosphere, there is a constantly flowing fountain, which causes some noise disturbance. The service at the beginning was very quick and attentive, giving a welcoming feeling. The language at the table occasionally switched between English and German, but that was not a major problem. The wine list is quite extensive, with a focus on German wines. Quite pricey, but that is to be expected with 2 stars. There are, however, a few wines under €100 that are worth trying.

The younger sommelier was a star, very helpful throughout the evening, with fine humor.
Unfortunately, we were not blown away by the vegetarian menu. The presentation was beautiful, but the flavors were sometimes a bit too sour and not surprising enough. It was also noticeable that all amuse-bouches and courses 1 through 5 were cold, while courses 6 and 7 were lukewarm (as intended). At this price level, things can and should be (much) better. Two dishes with peas in one menu is perhaps a bit much, and pea shoots were served on several courses. They are not tasty and serve only as garnish, but that is 'not done' in our eyes.

Our current rating is just barely 1 star, but the price level is equivalent to 2.5 stars.
Fortunately, the staff noticed our slight disappointment and we were compensated in a pleasant manner. Bravo for being open to constructive criticism.
Our advice regarding the vegetarian cuisine and the wine list: ensure innovation and be inspired by what is happening in the world.

The ambiance: FACIL, as a restaurant within the Mandala hotel, is perfectly situated: an oasis of calm and peace amidst the hustle and bustle of Potsdamer Platz. You sit in a glass pavilion surrounded by a bamboo garden, all on the fifth floor. It's brilliantly constructed. In good weather, the roof and walls open up, immersing you in nature – something almost unimaginable from outside the hotel. After dinner, you can easily return to one of the truly lovely rooms in just a few steps, without having to get in the car or a taxi. Perfect.

I'd like to end with a thought and the solution to a riddle you might not even know yet:

The thought – Even if fine dining is completely foreign to you, and you might have reservations because you "don't like it" or because of the cost, give it a try. Our greatest treasures are the memories we carry in our hearts, and which restaurant visit from ten years ago do you still remember? I alone will never forget that strawberry.

The answer – "Three and a half kilograms!" That's the answer to ONE question you'll ask yourself without a doubt during the evening. What question? You'll have to go there yourself to find out. Hehe.
